Cordially

KOR-jul-lee · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Cordially is in a warm and friendly manner.

Despite their sharp political disagreements, the two senators greeted each other cordially at the reception.

Worked Example

The hotel staff greeted every guest cordially, remembering names and asking about their trips home.

A genuinely warm, friendly welcome -- remembering names, asking real questions -- is exactly what cordially describes.

How Cordially Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

warmly

warmly: in a friendly, affectionate manner

amiably

amiably: in a friendly and pleasant way

Antonyms

coldly

coldly: without warmth or friendliness

curtly

curtly: in an abrupt, unfriendly manner

How Strong Is It? — politely → affectionately → cordially

politely vs. cordially

politely vs. cordially: Politely just means following good manners; cordially means genuinely warm and friendly, not just correctly behaved.

affectionately vs. cordially

affectionately vs. cordially: Affectionately can suggest an even deeper personal warmth than cordially, which usually describes a warm but still fairly formal greeting.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cord

root — cord: heart (Latin (cor, cordis))

suffix — -ial

suffix — -ial: pertaining to (Latin)

suffix — -ly

suffix — -ly: in a manner (English)

Put it together

Put it together: The root cord- ('heart,' from Latin cor/cordis) plus -ial ('pertaining to') plus -ly ('in a manner') gives 'from the heart' -- greeting someone cordially means welcoming them with genuine warmth.

Use the root in a new word: courage

Use the root in a new word: courage: Courage traces back to the same Latin cor ('heart') as cordially -- old French corage originally meant something closer to 'heart' or 'spirit.'

Root Check

Word Choice

Cordially describes genuine warmth in a greeting or interaction, distinct from mere politeness -- it appears often in formal invitations ('you are cordially invited') precisely because it signals real welcome, not just correct manners.
